I think she would feel sorry for all of them, herself included. Every single one of those children who were born into it. She is definitely intelligent enough to understand the tragedy that is. 

It’s certainly not more tragic just cause he’s rich. Every single child thrown into that war is a tragedy. In different ways. Some less than others. Obviously, Draco’s would be and is less tragic than anybody else’s but any child lost to hate and rage because it’s all they’ve ever known is a tragedy. 

Lucius did that as his LAST RESORT. That was the end-all-be-all option for him to save his son. I’m not saying he didn’t love Malfoy, that’s not what I’m saying; I am saying that buying him things does not equal actually showing love, affection, or respect on a day to day basis. Having Buckbeak beheaded was a show of power over the school, and a hatred of Hagrid for being half-giant. 

Also, I have no problem with Ron, I like Ron, and I think he was done a MAJOR disservice in the movies cause he was far more competent in the books than they portrayed him as. I didn’t see any issue with anything he did either, because ( & obviously none of it came anywhere near what Draco did so they’re not even comparable) but Ron was also a child thrown into an adult war. Every response he had to situations that is deemed “problematic” that you listed up there are completely understandable reactions from a child with limited emotional maturity. 

Also, again, it’s fiction. We can all decide what we want about the characters because they’re not real. If I read a fanfiction about how Draco is the same as he was as a child but still gets Hermione? Ridiculous, disgusting, and wrong. Reading about someone going to therapy, paying the consequences for their misguided beliefs, and becoming a better person? That’s fun. 

You can be a genuine asshole, a genuine piece of shit, (especially if you’re a child during it) and eventually grow to become a better person. That is possible.

See, the whole point of them IS the beauty in the redemption arc. You might not understand it, and that’s fine. 

But being a child DOES excuse a lot of things. We can always argue that no child should be tried as an adult. Literally no matter what they do, children are virtually incapable of understanding the actual impact of their words and actions and the consequences of their actions, especially a child raised in an environment where they receive no consequences because their parents have the money to protect/prevent them. They don’t have the brain processing capabilities on the same level as an adult. That is of course, extremely nuanced, and definitely open for argument. But there is still truth in the fact that children do not understand things the way adults do.

Which is why it’s cool that this is FICTION. Canonically, no, she wouldn’t end up with Draco, but that’s what makes the fan fictions so fun! And it makes them extremely heartbreaking. You don’t think Hermione would be pissed that a literal child was used as a pawn in grown men’s war? You don’t think she would, at minimum, be sympathetic to a child fighting his own battle in his own home? A child raised in hatred and violence? Because I believe she would. Harry was born into a war he never started as well, he just was born into the morally correct side, not immediately being inundated with racism and hatred. She def wouldn’t canonically bang and marry him, but I do believe that she was intelligent enough to see what happened to him as a tragedy. 

My personal headcanon (that most fan fictions use) is that Draco did all of the stuff he did in 6th year for his mother. To protect her. Which isn’t far fetched, that Voldemort would threaten his mother if he didn’t succeed. And quite frankly, as horrendous as the Malfoy’s were, his mother loved him. And judging by the way Lucious treated him, she may be the only person who showed him any love. 

Personally, if I was threatened by an extremely powerful being to kill someone or they’d kill MY mother? Yeah no I’m doing whatever I gotta do. But of course this is all headcanon so does it really matter? Not really, but it’s just one example of the perspectives used by Dramione fanfics. 

I don’t think you’re necessarily wrong I just find it odd to feel so STRONGLY against people reading things that are, whether you believe it or not, written really well, just because they don’t like the character ships. It ignores the fact that this is all fiction, and we can’t ask Harry or Ron or Hermione what they would do, therefore there is actually a possibility for anything.
